# Introduction

A fundamental theme in matrix analysis concerns the behavior of unitarily invariant norms under operator functions applied to sums and differences of positive semidefinite matrices. A cornerstone result in this direction is due to Ando and Zhan, who established that for positive semidefinite matrices $A$ and $B$, and for any non-negative operator monotone function $f$ on $[0,\infty)$, the inequality
$$
|||f(A) + f(B)||| \geq |||f(A+B)|||
$$
holds for every unitarily invariant norm $|||\cdot|||$. Complementing this, if $g$ denotes the operator monotone inverse of $f$ (so that $g$ is operator convex in the appropriate sense), the reverse inequality
$$
|||g(A) + g(B)||| \leq |||g(A+B)|||
$$
holds as well. These two inequalities have become foundational tools in the study of matrix inequalities, with applications ranging from operator theory to quantum information.

A natural and significant question is whether the operator monotonicity hypothesis on $f$ can be relaxed. This question was answered affirmatively in recent work by Bourin and Uchiyama, and independently by Kosem, who showed that the Ando–Zhan inequalities persist under the considerably weaker assumptions that $f$ is merely a non-negative concave function and $g$ is a non-negative convex function, without any operator-theoretic monotonicity or convexity requirements. This extension substantially broadens the class of functions to which the Ando–Zhan framework applies, encompassing many functions of practical interest that fail to be operator monotone or operator convex but remain concave or convex in the classical scalar sense.

Motivated by this generalization, the present paper turns to a related but distinct family of inequalities, also originally due to Ando, which concern differences rather than sums of positive semidefinite matrices. Specifically, for operator monotone $f$ and its inverse $g$, Ando proved that
$$
|||f(A) - f(B)||| \leq |||f(|A-B|)|||
$$
and
$$
|||g(A) - g(B)||| \geq |||g(|A-B|)|||.
$$
Given the successful extension of the sum inequalities to the broader class of concave and convex functions, it is natural to ask whether these difference inequalities admit a similar generalization: does the first inequality persist for arbitrary non-negative concave $f$, and does the second persist for arbitrary non-negative convex $g$, in place of their operator monotone counterparts?

The main contribution of this paper is a careful resolution of this question, revealing a more delicate situation than in the summation case. We demonstrate through explicit counterexamples that the naive generalization fails for general positive semidefinite matrices $A$ and $B$: neither inequality remains valid when $f$ is merely concave or $g$ merely convex, without further structural assumptions. This stands in sharp contrast to the Bourin–Uchiyama–Kosem extension of the Ando–Zhan sum inequalities, and it indicates that the mechanisms underlying the sum and difference inequalities are fundamentally different.

Despite this negative result in general, we identify an important special case in which the desired generalization does hold. Specifically, when the matrices satisfy the domination condition $A \geq \|B\|I$ — that is, when $A$ dominates $B$ in the operator order by at least the operator norm of $B$ — we prove that both inequalities extend successfully to arbitrary non-negative concave $f$ and convex $g$, respectively. This special case, while restrictive, arises naturally in several contexts and recovers the classical operator monotone results as a special instance.

To establish these results, and more broadly to shed new light on the structure underlying such inequalities, we introduce a new majorization-type relation between the eigenvalues of two Hermitian matrices, which we call $Y$-dominated majorisation. This notion refines classical weak majorization by incorporating an auxiliary matrix $Y$ that governs the comparison of spectra, and it captures precisely the structural condition needed to control the relevant unitarily invariant norm inequalities. We establish a key property of $Y$-dominated majorisation and demonstrate that this property not only yields our results on Ando's difference inequalities in the domination case $A \geq \|B\|I$, but also provides a unified and strengthened perspective on the existing Bourin–Uchiyama and Kosem theorems for the sum inequalities. In this way, the paper contributes both a clarification of the scope of Ando-type inequalities for concave and convex functions, and a new majorization technique of independent interest for the broader study of unitarily invariant norm inequalities.

# Extensions of Ando's Operator Monotone Inequalities via Y-Dominated Majorisation

## 1. Introduction

A fundamental theme in matrix analysis concerns the behavior of operator monotone and operator convex functions when applied to differences of positive semidefinite matrices. For two positive semidefinite matrices $A$ and $B$ acting on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, and for an operator monotone function $f:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ with $f(0)=0$, Ando's celebrated theorem asserts that

$$
|||f(A)-f(B)||| \leq |||f(|A-B|)|||
$$

holds for every unitarily invariant norm $|||\cdot|||$. This inequality has become a cornerstone result in the perturbation theory of matrix functions, with far-reaching consequences for the study of matrix means, entropy functionals, and quantum information measures.

A parallel and equally significant line of research addresses the additive counterpart of this inequality. Bourin and Uchiyama, building on earlier work in this direction, established that for non-negative concave functions $f$ on $[0,\infty)$ satisfying $f(0) = 0$, one has

$$
|||f(A+B)||| \leq |||f(A)+f(B)|||,
$$

while Kosem obtained the complementary inequality for convex functions with $f(0)=0$:

$$
|||f(A)+f(B)||| \leq |||f(A+B)|||.
$$

These sum-based inequalities hold for the broader classes of non-negative concave and convex functions, going beyond the operator monotone or operator convex requirement that appears in Ando's original theorem. This raises a natural and important question: does Ando's difference-based inequality admit a similar extension to non-negative concave and convex functions, or is the operator monotonicity assumption essential to its validity?

## 2. Main Results

In this paper, we investigate this question in detail and arrive at a nuanced answer. Our first result demonstrates that the naive extension of Ando's inequality to the class of non-negative concave (or convex) functions fails in general. Specifically, we construct explicit examples of positive semidefinite matrices $A$ and $B$ and a non-negative concave function $f$ with $f(0)=0$ for which

$$
|||f(A)-f(B)||| \leq |||f(|A-B|)|||
$$

fails to hold, even when $|||\cdot|||$ is taken to be the operator norm or the trace norm. This shows that operator monotonicity of $f$ cannot be dispensed with in complete generality, marking a genuine distinction between the additive and subtractive settings that was not previously understood.

Despite this negative result, we identify a natural structural condition under which the inequality does extend to the broader function classes. We show that if the matrices satisfy the domination condition $A \geq \|B\|I$ — meaning that $A$ dominates $B$ in the operator order by at least the operator norm of $B$ — then Ando's inequality

$$
|||f(A)-f(B)||| \leq |||f(|A-B|)|||
$$

holds for all non-negative concave functions $f$ with $f(0)=0$, and an analogous reversed inequality holds for non-negative convex functions. This condition, while restrictive, arises naturally in several operator-theoretic contexts and recovers the classical result in the special case where $f$ is operator monotone.

## 3. Y-Dominated Majorisation

The technical heart of our approach is a new majorisation concept that we introduce and call **Y-dominated majorisation**. This notion refines the classical weak majorisation framework used by Bourin-Uchiyama and Kosem by incorporating an auxiliary dominating structure $Y$ that controls the relationship between the eigenvalues of the matrices in question. We show that Y-dominated majorisation is a strictly stronger relation than ordinary weak log-majorisation of singular values, yet it remains tractable enough to be verified in the settings of interest.

Using this new tool, we are able not only to establish our positive result under the condition $A \geq \|B\|I$, but also to sharpen the original Bourin-Uchiyama and Kosem inequalities themselves. Specifically, we show that their sum-based inequalities can be derived as consequences of an underlying Y-dominated majorisation relation, which provides a unified and conceptually clearer explanation for why these inequalities hold for the full classes of non-negative concave and convex functions. This unification also yields new refinements: we obtain intermediate inequalities that interpolate between the classical bounds and provide additional information about the majorisation structure of $f(A)+f(B)$ relative to $f(A+B)$.

## 4. Structure of the Paper

The remainder of the paper is organized as follows. In Section 2, we recall the necessary background on unitarily invariant norms, majorisation, and the classical results of Ando, Bourin-Uchiyama, and Kosem. Section 3 presents our counterexamples showing the failure of Ando's inequality for general non-negative concave and convex functions. Section 4 introduces the concept of Y-dominated majorisation, establishes its basic properties, and proves our main positive result under the condition $A \geq \|B\|I$. Section 5 demonstrates how Y-dominated majorisation strengthens the Bourin-Uchiyama and Kosem inequalities, and discusses several corollaries and applications to matrix entropy inequalities. We conclude with a discussion of open problems, including the question of characterizing the full range of conditions on $A$ and $B$ under which Ando-type difference inequalities extend beyond the operator monotone class.

Whether Ando Zhan represents a person, a place, or perhaps a concept woven from cultural threads, the very structure of "for" implies purpose and intention. It is a dedication, a gift, an offering of thought or work directed toward a specific recipient.

Names carry stories within them. "Ando" evokes connections to Japanese heritage, perhaps referencing the renowned architect Tadao Ando, known for his minimalist concrete structures that play with light and shadow, creating spaces of contemplation and stillness. "Zhan" resonates with Chinese linguistic roots, meaning "to stand" or "to occupy"—a word suggesting presence, permanence, or perspective.

Together, these elements might represent a fusion—an intersection of cultures, disciplines, or ideas. Perhaps it is a title for a project, a piece of art, or a person who embodies qualities from multiple traditions: the contemplative minimalism suggested by "Ando" merged with the grounded stability of "Zhan."

# Abstract

Let $A$ and $B$ be positive semidefinite matrices, and let $f$ be a non-negative operator concave function on $[0,\infty)$ with $f(0) = 0$. Classical results of Ando and Zhan establish norm inequalities of the form $\|\|f(A+B)\|\| \leq \|\|f(A) + f(B)\|\|$ for all unitarily invariant norms, with a reverse-type inequality holding for operator convex functions. In this paper, we extend and refine these results in several directions. First, we generalize the Ando-Zhan inequality to a broader class of concave and convex functions, relaxing the operator concavity/convexity assumptions to weaker regularity conditions, and establish sharp constants governing the associated norm comparisons. Second, we introduce a new notion of *matrix majorization*, termed **weak block majorization**, which compares the eigenvalues of sums and direct sums of transformed matrices under a unified partial ordering framework. This concept strictly generalizes classical weak majorization and allows us to unify and strengthen several known inequalities, including those of Bourin-Uchiyama and Rotfel'd, within a single majorization-theoretic framework. Using this new majorization relation, we derive a family of norm inequalities that interpolate between the concave and convex cases, and we show that many previously known results emerge as special cases of our main theorems. We further explore applications to quantum entropy inequalities and to eigenvalue estimates for sums of positive semidefinite matrices, demonstrating that the weak block majorization technique yields sharper bounds than existing methods in several concrete examples. Finally, we discuss the limits of our approach by providing counterexamples showing that certain natural extensions to non-monotone or non-convex functions fail, thereby delineating the precise boundary of validity for Ando-Zhan type inequalities in the generalized setting.

# Abstract

Ando's inequality asserts that for Hermitian matrices $A, B$ and any operator monotone function $f:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ with $f(0)=0$, the operator norm inequality
$$
|||f(A) - f(B)||| \le |||f(|A-B|)|||
$$
holds for every unitarily invariant norm $|||\cdot|||$. This work investigates the extent to which such a comparison persists when the operator monotonicity hypothesis is relaxed to the strictly weaker condition that $f$ is merely operator concave (or, dually, operator convex) on $[0,\infty)$.

We show that the naive extension fails in general: concavity/convexity alone does not guarantee the norm inequality for arbitrary unitarily invariant norms, and we exhibit explicit low-dimensional counterexamples using $2\times 2$ and $3\times 3$ matrices where the eigenvalue rearrangement forced by concavity produces a majorization relation incompatible with Ando-type domination. This clarifies the special role that monotonicity plays in controlling the *sign* structure of $f(A)-f(B)$ relative to $A-B$, a feature that concavity alone does not supply.

To recover a positive theory, we introduce the notion of **$Y$-dominated majorization**: given a fixed positive operator (or fixed reference matrix) $Y$, we say that a Hermitian $X$ is *$Y$-dominated* if the eigenvalues of $X$ are weakly majorized by those of $Y$ after an order-preserving rearrangement compatible with the spectral decomposition of $Y$, i.e.
$$
\sum_{i=1}^{k}\lambda_i^{\downarrow}(X) \le \sum_{i=1}^{k}\lambda_i^{\downarrow}(Y), \qquad k=1,\dots,n,
$$
together with a compatibility condition linking the eigenprojections of $X$ and $Y$. This notion is designed to capture exactly the residual structural information that survives when operator monotonicity is weakened to concavity: while $f(A)-f(B)$ need not be dominated by $f(|A-B|)$ in the strong (unitarily invariant norm) sense, it *is* $f(|A-B|)$-dominated in this weaker majorization sense, for a suitable class of operator concave $f$.

Using this framework we prove:

1. **A majorization-level Ando inequality for concave functions.** If $f$ is operator concave and $f(0)\ge 0$, then $f(A)-f(B)$ is $f(|A-B|)$-dominated in the sense above, and consequently
$$
|||f(A)-f(B)||| \le |||f(|A-B|)|||
$$
holds for all *symmetric gauge* (Ky Fan dominated) norms, even though it may fail for general unitarily invariant norms.

2. **Sharpness.** We show the symmetric gauge restriction is necessary: the counterexamples above involve unitarily invariant norms outside this class.

3. **Convex case duality.** An analogous $Y$-dominated majorization statement holds for operator convex $f$ with $f(0)\le 0$, with the inequality reversing direction in the appropriate sense (sub-majorization becomes super-majorization).

4. **Applications.** We derive new perturbation bounds for concave/convex operator functions (e.g., $f(t)=t^p$, $0<p<1$ or $1<p<2$; $f(t)=\log(1+t)$) that were previously accessible only via the monotone case or via weaker Lipschitz-type estimates, and we connect the $Y$-dominated majorization order to existing partial orders (Hardy–Littlewood–Pólya majorization, weak log-majorization) used in quantum information and matrix perturbation theory.

These results delineate precisely how much of Ando's phenomenon is attributable to monotonicity versus concavity, and the $Y$-dominated majorization framework offers a flexible tool for extending norm comparison inequalities beyond the classical operator monotone setting.

# Abstract

Let $A$ and $B$ be positive semidefinite matrices. Classical results due to Ando, Zhan, Bourin-Uchiyama, and Kosem have established fundamental unitarily invariant norm inequalities comparing $\||A+B|\|$, $\||A^r + B^r|\|^{1/r}$, and related expressions involving sums, products, and powers of positive semidefinite matrices. These results play a central role in matrix analysis, with applications extending to quantum information theory, operator theory, and the study of matrix means.

In this paper, we extend this circle of ideas by introducing a new majorization relation that refines and unifies several known inequalities. Specifically, we establish that for positive semidefinite matrices $A, B$ and appropriate parameters, a sharper eigenvalue majorization holds, from which a family of unitarily invariant norm inequalities—including trace norm and operator norm estimates as special cases—can be derived. Our approach relies on a combination of variational principles for eigenvalues, integral representations of matrix functions, and antisymmetric tensor power techniques.

We show that our majorization result recovers, as special cases, the inequalities of Bourin-Uchiyama and Kosem, while also yielding new sharper bounds in regimes not covered by previous methods. Furthermore, we discuss the sharpness of our results by providing examples showing that the majorization cannot be improved in general. Applications to norm inequalities for sums and differences of positive operators, as well as connections to the Ando-Zhan conjecture-type problems, are also discussed.

Our results contribute new tools to the study of operator inequalities and offer a unified framework for understanding majorization phenomena for positive semidefinite matrices under unitarily invariant norms.

# Abstract

Ando's celebrated inequalities characterize operator monotone and operator convex functions through matrix majorization and unitarily invariant norm comparisons involving positive semidefinite matrices. This work investigates whether these classical inequalities persist when the strong hypothesis of operator monotonicity or operator convexity is relaxed to the weaker, more broadly applicable conditions of ordinary non-negative concavity or convexity on Hermitian matrices. We examine, for pairs of positive semidefinite matrices $A, B$ and non-negative concave (respectively convex) functions $f$, the extent to which inequalities of the form
$$
f(A+B) \leq f(A) + f(B) \quad \text{(concave case)}
$$
or their convex counterparts continue to hold in the sense of weak majorization or unitarily invariant norms, without assuming the full operator-theoretic monotonicity structure. Our central contribution is a novel majorization technique based on a refined eigenvalue interlacing and block-decomposition argument, which allows direct comparison of eigenvalue sequences of $f(A+B)$, $f(A)$, and $f(B)$ under only scalar-level concavity or convexity assumptions on $f$. This tool circumvents the need for integral representations of operator monotone functions traditionally employed in Ando-type proofs, and instead exploits a compression and pinching scheme adapted to the spectral geometry of $A + B$. Using this technique, we establish that Ando-type norm inequalities remain valid for a substantial class of non-negative concave functions, including piecewise smooth and non-analytic examples excluded from the operator monotone class, while we identify sharp counterexamples showing that the convex case admits only a restricted analogue, requiring an additional sub-additivity or normalization condition on $f$. We further discuss the implications of these results for entropy-type and trace-functional inequalities in quantum information theory, where operator convexity assumptions are often stronger than necessary. The findings suggest a broader majorization-theoretic framework in which classical operator inequalities of Ando, Bourin, and Uchiyama can be recovered as special cases, while extending their applicability to a wider class of matrix functions relevant in numerical linear algebra and mathematical physics.

# Abstract

Let $A$ and $B$ be positive semidefinite matrices, and let $f$ be a nonnegative concave function on $[0,\infty)$ with $f(0) = 0$. A celebrated inequality of Ando states that for any unitarily invariant norm $\|\cdot\|$,
$$\|f(A+B)\| \leq \|f(A) + f(B)\|.$$
In this paper, we investigate extensions of this inequality to the setting where $A$ and $B$ are replaced by arbitrary matrices $X$ and $Y$, and the sum $A+B$ is replaced by more general combinations, motivated by questions of majorization and the theory of operator monotone and operator convex functions.

We introduce a new notion of majorization, which we call *majorization dominated by a matrix $Y$*, designed to interpolate between weak majorization of singular values and stronger operator-theoretic comparisons. Precisely, we say that the singular values of a matrix $X$ are majorized by those of a matrix $Z$, dominated by $Y$, if
$$\sum_{i=1}^{k} s_i(X) \leq \sum_{i=1}^{k} s_i(Z) + c\, s_1(Y), \quad k = 1, 2, \dots,$$
for a suitable constant $c$ depending on the structural data, where $s_i(\cdot)$ denotes the $i$-th singular value. This notion allows us to formulate and prove generalized Ando-type inequalities of the form
$$\|f(X^*X + Y^*Y)\| \preceq_Y \|f(X^*X) + f(Y^*Y)\|$$
for concave $f$, and dual inequalities for convex $f$ with reversed order, where $\preceq_Y$ denotes majorization dominated by $Y$.

We establish several positive results: for concave functions $f$ vanishing at $0$, and for a broad class of convex functions satisfying mild growth conditions, the generalized inequality holds for all unitarily invariant norms under appropriate dominance by $Y$. We further show that these results are sharp by constructing explicit counterexamples demonstrating that the inequality fails, in general, when the dominance term is removed or when $f$ fails to satisfy the stated convexity/concavity hypotheses. In particular, we exhibit matrices $X, Y$ and unitarily invariant norms for which the naive extension of Ando's inequality (without the correction term governed by $Y$) is violated, clarifying the necessity of our majorization framework.

As applications, we recover several known norm inequalities as special cases, derive new inequalities for the operator absolute value and for sums of matrix powers, and discuss connections with the Rotfel'd trace inequality and its unitarily invariant norm analogues. Our results shed new light on the delicate interplay between operator convexity/concavity and majorization in matrix analysis, and provide a unified framework encompassing both positive and negative instances of Ando-type inequalities.
